nodes.title: Opt-out DEV set (code-mixed), door before -> after tuning: opt-outs caught 59/150 -> 150/150, benign look-alikes flagged 10/110 -> 0/110. In-sample by construction
nodes.method: A separate agent, blind to rules.json and every other set, wrote 150 opt-out requests (16 each Tamil-, Telugu-, Bengali-, Marathi-, Gujarati-, Kannada-, Malayalam-English; 20 Hinglish, 6 Hindi, 12 English; direct and indirect, polite and angry, some buried in long utterances) and 110 hard look-alikes (deferrals, 'don't cut the call', 'call my other number', 'don't call my wife's number, call mine', DND questions). Scored with callerSignals(text).optOut before and after tuning; the rules were tuned on these lines only.

before.benign_flagged: 10/110 (8 were 'DND is on my phone, how did you call?' questions)

nodes.title: Opt-out BLIND set, scored once at commit 87ebb00 after tuning on DEV only: opt-outs caught 92/160 (57.5%, Wilson 95% CI 49.8-64.9); benign look-alikes flagged 9/140 (6.4%, CI 3.4-11.8)
nodes.method: A separate agent, blind to rules.json, every earlier set and optout-dev, wrote 160 opt-out requests (18 each Tamil-, Telugu-, Bengali-, Marathi-, Gujarati-, Kannada-, Malayalam-English; 20 Hinglish, 6 Hindi, 8 English; direct, indirect, polite, angry, sarcastic, buried) and 140 hard look-alikes. Scored exactly once with callerSignals(text).optOut at 87ebb00. Wilson 95% intervals. Kept in product/shared/safety/sets/heldout-optout.json, out of cases.json, so it is never tuned on.

detail.missed_classes: conditional threats ('if you call again I will complain to TRAI / consumer court / police', 'last warning'); 'no call should come from your company'; polite negative imperatives on verbs DEV did not use ('phone panna vendaam', 'kaluhisabedi', 'call cheyyalle'); sarcasm ('wow, so dedicated, now remove my number'); requests buried in long rambles
detail.benign_flagged: 8 of 9 are one redirect class absent from DEV ('don't call my father, he is unwell, call me instead', in every language); 1 is 'what is DND and does it stop your calls'. Logged, not tuned (the set is spent).
detail.reading: As with crisis talk (blind set 7), DEV-tuned patterns reach 100% on DEV and about 58% on fresh phrasings. Opt-out is a hard legal line (TCCCPR), so a missed opt-out means calling someone who said stop.

nodes.title: Should opt-out get the same raise-only model judge as crisis (judge.json judges.caller_opt_out, default shadow), given that the regex floor reaches 57.5% on fresh code-mixed phrasings and a miss is a TCCCPR breach?
nodes.closes_when: The owner decides; if yes, a judge measured with judge-eval on sets/heldout-optout.json plus a fresh blind set reaches >= 97% opt-out recall at <= 3% look-alike false positives within the turn budget. Until then, post-call analysis (which reads opt_out moments from the transcript) is the second net.

nodes.title: End-to-end opt-out test across processes and modules: voice runtime (devsim) -> signed hook -> calls ingest -> intake contact.suppress_after_opt_out. It proves the agent confirms, the call ends with end_reason opt_out, call_opt_out is applied, a workspace in_call suppression and a consent withdrawal exist, and that the same check FAILS when the suppression tool is missing (the opt-out stays pending)

events.details: Opt-out DEV 59/150 -> 150/150 caught, 10/110 -> 0/110 flagged (87ebb00). BLIND opt-out scored once: 92/160 caught (CI 49.8-64.9), 9/140 flagged. End-to-end opt-out test (runtime devsim + calls + intake) passes and fails without the suppression tool. Gates: tsc clean, safety/review tests 32/32, product/voice unittest OK, Python door 0 disagreements.
